output.brief: Please hold the breach notice. The evidence points away from Tessaly's crews and toward the tag stock. Since 1 September, Corvane's bags printed at Harlow Bay check-in have failed automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% in August. Corvane transfer bags and Pelion bags, which use the same Tessaly crew pool and the same readers, stayed at about 1.4% and 1.3%. Pelion's mishandling rate did not move. On 14–16 October, counters that used Brackwater stock from stores failed at 1.6%, while kiosks printing the new Fennick stock failed at 12.1%. Unreadable bags go to the manual encode desk, wait about 30 minutes there, and arrive after the lateral has closed. Bags on the automatic path stayed at about 3.8 per 1,000. Whether the cause is the Fennick media or the printer heat setting is not yet established, so a defect claim against Fennick would be premature. Next steps: switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater stock now, since five weeks are held in stores and the contract runs to 31 December. Then test the Fennick stock against the printer settings. Consider a temporary extra encode workstation in the evening bank. Tessaly's inexperienced crews are a separate point to follow up through the retraining plan. I'm fairly confident, about 80%.
